description:
Chromeworks did not want to make digitigrade legs. The Reverie exists because their design team was approached repeatedly by body-modification subculture clients who wanted Chromeworks' neural integration quality in a non-human chassis, and eventually the revenue argument won. The result is Chromeworks' signature seamless chrome aesthetic applied to a reverse-knee digitigrade frame — mirror-polished surfaces, flush panel seams, and an optional bioluminescent vein option that traces the joint lines in selectable color. Functionally they are mid-tier: faster than stock human legs, capable of a 3-meter vertical, but the engineering priority was appearance and neural fidelity, not performance.

The Reverie is the body-mod subculture's aspirational object precisely because it is beautiful and wrong at the same time. Wearers are not trying to pass — they are trying to be seen, to make the alienness gorgeous, to force the discomfort into something that cannot look away. Chromeworks quietly markets them only through specialty boutiques and does not feature them in mainline advertising, but the waiting list is real. The stigma is the point. The mirror finish makes sure you notice.
